Overview Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary is a multidenominational, evangelical graduate school committed to equipping Christian leaders to think theologically, engage globally, and live biblically. With nearly 1,400 students across campuses in Massachusetts, North Carolina, Florida, and online, Gordon-Conwell’s student body represents more than eighty-five denominations and fifty countries. The seminary offers master’s and doctoral programs—delivered in English, Spanish, and Portuguese—that combine academic excellence, spiritual formation, and a deep commitment to Scripture. Its 12,000 alumni serve Christ through ministry in the church, the academy, and the workplace. Gordon-Conwell is accredited by the Association of Theological Schools, the New England Commission of Higher Education, and the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs. Position Summary Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (www.gordonconwell.edu) announces a faculty position in the area of preaching with the primary location at the Hamilton campus. This position is for any rank from Assistant up to the Haddon Robinson Chair of Preaching. This is a continuing-status track appointment with an expected start date of July 1, 2026, or as soon as possible after the position is filled. The successful candidate for this position should have extensive experience in the pulpit as well as a track record of excellence in classroom teaching and effectiveness in preparing students for preaching and pastoral ministry in the ‘Big Idea’ tradition of Haddon Robinson. The candidate should be a gifted researcher and have several significant contributions to theologically related scholarship and/or leadership in the life of the church. This position entails considerable leadership outside the classroom in the ongoing task of forming students for the preaching call. The professor holding this position will be expected to participate in the life of the seminary through weekly Chapel worship and advising, mentoring and discipleship activities with students. The ideal candidate will be skilled at envisioning and organizing programs and continuing education events for alumni pastors. The professor’s teaching responsibilities will be primarily at the Hamilton Campus (in-person and digital), with an expectation that the professor will teach at our Charlotte campus annually. The professor will be expected to teach Masters level courses as well as supervise and teach in the Doctor of Ministry program as well as our anticipated PhD program. Life Together (Hamilton Campus) The Hamilton Campus of Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary is invested in a “Life Together” ethos of education that prioritizes presence, intentionality, and relationships. Faculty and students are encouraged to engage in rhythms of prayer, worship, and fellowship, as well as intentional discipleship relationships.[1] The ideal candidate will be committed to investing time in personal mentoring/discipleship of our students. Academic Experience The person seeking this position should hold a graduate degree in theology (MDiv preferable) and a Ph.D. in a subject relevant to homiletics. Scholarly participation in the field through publication is expected. Experience with theological education and pastoral ministry is very important. Personal Profile The applicant should be a person of Christian character and be at home in the thoughtful evangelical ethos of Gordon-Conwell. The person should be manifestly collegial in their relationships, demonstrating an ability to work well with colleagues who represent various ecclesial traditions and ethnic backgrounds. The person should be attentive to different cultures, being able to serve both our local New England context and our growing international student body

job_3870413c8ee0af8f: Overview Have you ever wondered why higher education feels stuck? Or imagined rebuilding it from the ground up? Imagine a university where advanced technology enhances every student's learning experience through personalized, adaptive, and real-world education. San Francisco Bay University (SFBU), an innovative, nonprofit, WASC-accredited university located in the heart of Silicon Valley, seeks a forward-thinking and experienced Online Adjunct Professor of Accounting to teach ACC 501 Managerial Accounting within our MBA Pro+ program. Working alongside innovative instructional technologies, including artificial intelligence-enhanced learning tools, the faculty member will guide graduate students through engaging asynchronous learning experiences while providing the mentorship, coaching, and academic oversight that only expert faculty can deliver. The MBA Pro+ program prepares current and aspiring business leaders with the financial and managerial knowledge needed to succeed in today's technology-driven global economy. Accounting serves as the foundation for sound business decision-making, while emerging technologies and artificial intelligence continue to transform financial reporting, auditing, compliance, and business analytics. Students learn to interpret financial statements, apply accounting principles, evaluate financial performance, analyze managerial accounting information, understand auditing and regulatory requirements, and leverage modern accounting technologies to solve complex business challenges. Through executive case studies, simulations, and applied consulting projects, graduates develop the analytical, ethical, and strategic skills necessary to support organizational accountability and long-term success. What You Bring We are looking for educators who are passionate about graduate business education and committed to preparing the next generation of accounting professionals. Ideal candidates have experience designing engaging, student-centered learning experiences that foster analytical thinking, ethical decision-making, and practical application of accounting principles. Candidates should be interested in exploring how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are reshaping accounting practice and business education and be excited to contribute to a culture of continuous innovation within the MBA Pro+ program. The Department holds a strong intellectual commitment to innovative interdisciplinary approaches to film and media research, evidenced in the scholarship of its thirteen current ladder faculty, five of whom have officially shared appointments with other departments in the Division of Arts & Humanities. The position will include teaching, research, and service to support the production of experimental and avant-garde cinema or experimentation in and across genre forms, potentially including narrative. The aim of the Film and Media Department’s production program is to teach students the grammar of cinema and how to use it to experiment with forms of self-expression, historical investigation, and aesthetic analysis, among others. The Assistant Professor in Film and Video Production will convey to students creative approaches to low-budget, small crews, street-level production, a capacious understanding of what can be achieved beyond Hollywood, and an understanding of film production as a means of generating new, critical, and experimental media theory and history.  Position Summary Postdoctoral Research Associate positions are available in the Shmuylovich Laboratory at WashU Medicine. Our lab develops and translates novel optical imaging technologies for noninvasive diagnosis and monitoring of human disease, with a particular focus on skin imaging across the full spectrum of skin pigmentation. We combine biomedical optics, multispectral and infrared imaging, spectroscopy, image processing, computational analysis, and clinical investigation to develop technologies that can improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce disparities in care. Current projects span visible, near-infrared, and short-wave infrared imaging and include applications in dermatology, vascular disease, tissue injury, and physiologic monitoring. The laboratory works at the intersection of engineering, physics, computation, and clinical medicine, with opportunities to participate in device development, optical system design, image and signal analysis, translational studies, and human-subject research. Postdoctoral researchers will have the opportunity to lead independent projects while working closely with a multidisciplinary team of clinicians, engineers, physicists, and collaborators across WashU and other institutions. We are particularly interested in creative and highly motivated scientists who enjoy solving technically challenging problems with a clear path toward clinical translation. Trainees will be encouraged to develop their own research ideas, publish their work, present at national meetings, and pursue independent funding and career-development opportunities. The Shmuylovich Laboratory is based within the Department of Dermatology at WashU Medicine in St. Louis and benefits from the institution’s extensive resources in biomedical engineering, imaging, clinical research, and translational medicine.
